newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Sun Hung Kai halts gold market-making.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Sun Hung Kai halts gold market-making.

text.p: Frustrated by moribund gold prices Sun Hung Kai Bullion Ltd has decided to pull-out of market-making from September onwards, but may be persuaded back should volatility improve, a company official said on Thursday.
"We will temporarily stop being a market maker in bullion," executive director Gary Cheung, told Reuters by telephone.
Cheung said his company was not losing confidence in the gold market, but the business did not justify Sun Hung Kai's position as a market maker.
A paucity of dealers in Hong Kong -- as well as in Singapore and Sydney -- meant a single large order could move the market, Cheung said.
"Before, when there were more dealers around, (the market) could sustain these sort of orders because the orders could be spread around to all the dealers," he noted.
Sun Hung Kai will still quote prices to its customers on a 24-hour basis, as well as continue to deal in physical gold, silver, platinum, and base metals.
"We are more inclined towards customer-oriented business rather than the interbank business," Cheung said.
Should the market pick-up, Sun Hung Kai can redeploy dealers back into its bullion business, Cheung added, noting that no employees were being laid off.
Sun Hung Kai has recently sent out letters informing all its counterparties of the company's change in strategy, Cheung said.
Gold dealers said the move would not have much impact on the local market.
Sun Hung Kai Bullion Ltd is a subsidiary of Hong Kong-listed conglomerate Sun Hung Kai and Company Ltd..
